final_candidates.decision_summary: Buried, fully conserved glycine in the catalytic (β/α)8 barrel with the highest catalytic-domain LOF proxy (AM 0.962) and essentially zero ESM-1v plausibility; a β-branched Val cannot be accommodated at a backbone-flexible Gly, predicting complete loss of activity.

Buried hydrophobic core Leu in the catalytic domain replaced by a charged Arg (AM 0.926, ESM-1v ~0), a classic fold-disrupting substitution. Mechanistic reasoning and both evidence dimensions agree on abolished catalysis.

Conserved catalytic-domain glycine with full MSA coverage and zero Val frequency among homologs; AM 0.911 places it in the strongly pathogenic tier, and the bulky β-branched substitution should disrupt the FAD-binding barrel. Preferred over the higher-AM P572R because the regulatory-domain site may act by destabilization/SAM regulation rather than abolishing catalysis.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence across phenotype proxy, MSA, and PLM is consistent and further tool calls would not change the Top-3 ordering.

history.rationale: Arg157 (verified R at 157) is a strictly conserved FAD/substrate-contacting arginine in the catalytic TIM-barrel; R157Q is a recognized severe MTHFR-deficiency allele with near-null activity.
The proxy substitution R157C scored only 0.671 (lowest of the tested set), suggesting position 157 tolerates substitution better than the barrel-core positions; demoted but retained.
AM 0.629 is the second-lowest in the pool and the conservative Arg→Gln change is unlikely to abolish catalysis; removed to free a slot.

rejection.reason: AM 0.629 is the second-lowest in the pool and the conservative Arg→Gln change is unlikely to abolish catalysis; removed to free a slot.

history.rationale: Thr227 (verified T) lies in the conserved barrel core near the FAD site; T227M is a classic severe-deficiency substitution causing gross loss of catalytic activity and thermolability.
Clinically documented severe MTHFR deficiency allele with near-null residual activity; not yet tested, so kept at high rank pending phenotype evidence.
AM only 0.671 — pathogenic class but well below the 0.9+ tier, consistent with the clinical picture of severe-but-residual activity; demoted out of contention.
Arg335 (verified R) is a buried conserved charged residue in the catalytic domain; R335C is a reported severe loss-of-function allele that removes a key salt bridge.
Reported severe-deficiency arginine in the catalytic domain; untested, retained for the next phenotype query.
AM classifies it benign (0.109) despite the mutant residue being absent from homologs; the LOF-proxy tool is the closest dimension to the reward, so this candidate is dropped.

rejection.reason: AM classifies it benign (0.109) despite the mutant residue being absent from homologs; the LOF-proxy tool is the closest dimension to the reward, so this candidate is dropped.

history.rationale: Gly149 (verified G) sits in a tight conserved barrel turn where only glycine is tolerated; a beta-branched Val is expected to sterically break the fold and abolish activity.
Position 149 intolerance is corroborated by G149R, but Val is a smaller perturbation, so it is kept below the Arg variant.
AM 0.911 (pathogenic) plus zero Val frequency at a fully covered, conserved catalytic-domain glycine; promoted from rank 9 to the top tier as a strong backup.
Pro572 (verified P) is in the conserved C-terminal SAM-regulatory domain; P572L is a documented severe-deficiency mutation impairing enzyme function/stability.
Position 572 is confirmed highly intolerant by the P572R evidence, but Leu is a milder chemical change so it ranks below P572R.
Leu is the natural residue at position 572 in ~31% of aligned homologs, which directly undercuts a null phenotype; P572R covers the same position with a more disruptive, non-observed residue.

rejection.reason: Leu is the natural residue at position 572 in ~31% of aligned homologs, which directly undercuts a null phenotype; P572R covers the same position with a more disruptive, non-observed residue.

history.rationale: Arg183 (verified R) is a conserved surface/interface arginine in the catalytic domain likely forming a stabilizing ion pair; charge loss is predicted to be strongly destabilizing.
Conservative Arg→Gln at a surface-exposed arginine; the weak R157C result suggests such Arg positions are less reliably null than core/Gly/Pro sites.

rejection.reason: Conservative Arg→Gln at a surface-exposed arginine; the weak R157C result suggests such Arg positions are less reliably null than core/Gly/Pro sites.

history.rationale: Arg377 (verified R) is conserved in the catalytic/linker region and reported as a disease-associated substitution; Cys removes the charge and can add an unpaired thiol.
Same rationale as R183Q — surface Arg substitutions gave the weakest damaging signal, and pool slots are better spent on core-disrupting variants.

rejection.reason: Same rationale as R183Q — surface Arg substitutions gave the weakest damaging signal, and pool slots are better spent on core-disrupting variants.

history.rationale: Gly255 (verified G in the conserved 'IVPGIFP' motif) is a backbone-flexibility glycine in the barrel; introducing a bulky charged Arg should sterically block the active-site loop.
Superseded by G255V, which was directly measured with a very high LOF proxy; keeping both wastes a slot at the same position.

rejection.reason: Superseded by G255V, which was directly measured with a very high LOF proxy; keeping both wastes a slot at the same position.

history.rationale: Leu323 (verified L) is within a conserved helix following the HFYT motif; proline insertion should break the helix and unfold the catalytic domain.
Superseded by the directly measured L323R at the same position; one representative per position is sufficient given the small budget.

rejection.reason: Superseded by the directly measured L323R at the same position; one representative per position is sufficient given the small budget.

history.rationale: Ala222 (verified A) is the classic C677T thermolabile variant reducing activity ~50-70%; included as a benchmark but likely only partial, not complete, loss of function.
Common thermolabile polymorphism retaining substantial catalytic activity — clearly not an activity-abolishing variant.

rejection.reason: Common thermolabile polymorphism retaining substantial catalytic activity — clearly not an activity-abolishing variant.
